newsitem.title: UK: Iraq asks Spain to help Uday Hussein -- opposition.
newsitem.headline: Iraq asks Spain to help Uday Hussein -- opposition.

text.p: An Iraqi opposition group said on Thursday that Baghdad had asked Spain to provide medical treatment for Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, who was injured in an assassination attempt last December.
The London-based Iraqi Broadcast Corporation (IBC) said Iraq had made the request through a former Spanish intelligence officer who visited Baghdad recently.
IBC said in a statement that doctors, faced with the task of removing two bullets from Uday's spine, felt the operation was so delicate that it had to be carried out abroad.
Uday Hussein said in a CNN interview shown last week that he was mentally and physically normal after the attack, which he said had been carried out by Iranians.
He said he had been hit in various parts of the body, including both his legs, and added that Iraqi and French surgeons would shortly operate on his left leg.
He also said that he had already undergone surgery to remove a bullet and pieces of shrapnel from his body.
